Status
Current state: Under Discussion
Discussion thread:https://lists.apache.org/thread/0frtc6h3y9ts89do3qb9yk6oj3o1ktg2
JIRA:KAFKA-18800
Target release: 4.5
Please keep the discussion on the mailing list rather than commenting on the wiki (wiki discussions get unwieldy fast).
Motivation
Authorizer#aclCount()was added byKIP-801(PR #11649, Kafka 3.2) so that the broker could publish anAclCountmetric by reading the value from the authorizer. The broker side of that plan was never implemented.
KIP-877later introducedMonitorable/PluginMetrics, which lets every plugin register its own metrics. Authorizers gained that support in 4.1 (KAFKA-18888,PR #19050), andStandardAuthorizernow publishesacls-total-countthroughPluginMetrics, backed by exactly the same data asAuthorizer#aclCount().
WithPluginMetricsavailable,Authorizer#aclCount()no longer has a purpose, so this KIP deprecates it. Third-party authorizers that want an ACL-count metric, or any other metric, should implementMonitorableper KIP-877.
Public Interfaces
Authorizer#aclCount()is marked@Deprecated(forRemoval = true).java
No other public API changes. Theacls-total-countmetric name, type, and tag set produced byStandardAuthorizerare unchanged.
Proposed Changes
DeprecateAuthorizer#aclCount()in 4.5 and remove it in 5.0.
Make theacls-total-countgauge inStandardAuthorizerread the count fromStandardAuthorizerDatadirectly instead of callingaclCount(). The metric value does not change.
Remove StandardAuthorizer#aclCount()in 4.5.
Compatibility, Deprecation, and Migration Plan
Authorizer#aclCount()stays on the interface with the same signature and the same-1default, so existing authorizers keep compiling and running. The only visible effect is a deprecation warning.
No metric changes for anyone.StandardAuthorizerkeeps publishingacls-total-countunder the same name and tags, and since the broker never usedAuthorizer#aclCount(), third-party authorizers never had a metric derived from it.
A third-party authorizer can define its own metrics throughMonitorable(supported for authorizers since 4.1). It does not need to follow the metric names used byStandardAuthorizer. For example:javajava
The deprecation will be listed in the 4.5 upgrade notes, and the method will be removed in Kafka 5.0.
Test Plan
PR #23521(merged) added a unit test for theacls-total-countmetric. It does not depend on this KIP.
Rejected Alternatives
KeepAuthorizer#aclCount()as is.The broker never reads it, so keeping it could mislead third-party implementations.
Finish the KIP-801 plan by having the broker publish anAclCountmetric fromaclCount().This is no longer needed, because authorizers can now register their own metrics throughPluginMetrics(KIP-877).
